statement: Processing of personal data is lawful only if and to the extent that at least one of the Article 6(1) bases applies: the data subject's consent for one or more specific purposes; necessity for the performance of a contract with the data subject or for pre-contractual steps at the data subject's request; compliance with a legal obligation; protection of vital interests; performance of a task carried out in the public interest or in the exercise of official authority; or the legitimate interests of the controller or a third party, except where overridden by the data subject's interests or fundamental rights and freedoms, in particular where the data subject is a child (GDPR Article 6(1)(a)-(f)).
caveat: The legitimate-interests basis is unavailable to public authorities in the performance of their tasks (Art. 6(1), final subparagraph), member-state law can add specificity for the legal-obligation and public-task bases, consent carries the separate Article 7 conditions, and special categories of data are governed by Article 9 on top of Article 6. Verified against the Official Journal text on the Publications Office cellar (eur-lex.europa.eu was unreachable to automated fetches at check time). This repo does not select a lawful basis.
